summary: Deploy 'claim-broker' flow: delegated Slack namespace claim + timebound access + Confluence project seeding
description:
Issue summary:
We need a production-ready 'claim-broker' service that lets internal teams request and claim a pre-approved Slack namespace (channel prefix + template) with timebound access. When a claim is approved, the system should provision a Confluence space seeded with the team's templates, attach a Jira project stub (optional), and emit audit snapshots to S3 for compliance.

Impact:
- Faster pod onboarding (goal: reduce manual provisioning by 70%).
- Keeps access timebound to reduce lingering privileges.
- Provides audit trail for security/compliance.

Requirements / Acceptance criteria:
1) Self-service portal (web form or Slack modal) for claim requests with reason, owner, TTL (default 90 days).
2) Approval webhook to designated approver group; approvals must be recorded in Jira as a compact audit entry.
3) On approval: create Slack channel namespace and invite owner/service-accounts with ephemeral membership (SCIM/Okta integration preferred).
4) Seed a Confluence space with team templates and initial 'runbook' page; permissions mirror team owners.
5) Emit a signed audit snapshot (JSON + SHA256) to S3 and create a retention policy entry.
6) Provide a 'renew' and 'relinquish' flow handling TTL extension and proactive expiry notifications.
7) Configurable guardrails: deny if sensitive data tag present, require security review for vendor-facing namespaces.

Environment:
prod (primary), staging for initial rollout; target regions: us-west, eu-west.

Steps to validate in staging:
1) Open Slack modal via /claim-namespace (staging bot) and submit sample request for "team-signal" prefix.
2) Approver in group 'pod-admins' receives Slack approval DM and web console notification.
3) Approve request; verify Slack namespace created with proper naming and default channels (#team-signal-general, #team-signal-ops).
4) Confirm Confluence space created at /spaces/TEAM-SIGNAL with seeded runbook page.
5) Check S3 bucket s3://redwood-internal-audits/claims/ for audit snapshot and SHA256 file.
6) Trigger TTL expiry simulation and confirm notification flow to owners and automated archival proposal.

Observed errors / logs (staging):
- 2026-03-04T15:12:02Z ERROR claim-broker.lambda create_confluence_space 403 Forbidden: API key rejected (service-account lacking 'space:create').
- 2026-03-04T15:12:05Z WARN claim-broker.lambda invite_scim Okta throttling: 429 (retry-after: 30s).
- Sample webhook payload (redacted): {
  "request_id": "cb-20260304-7f3a",
  "prefix": "team-signal",
  "owner": "m.chen@redwood.ai",
  "ttl_days": 90
}

Notes: scope of work intentionally excludes full SSO integration for external partners — that will be follow-up.
comments: 2026-03-05 - Maya Chen (Reporter): Creating ticket to formalize the claim-broker scope. PoC succeeded in hackweek but needs prod hardening: scoping, auditing, and TTL enforcement.

2026-03-06 - Arjun Patel (Assignee): Triage complete — initial checklist attached. Need service account grants for Confluence space creation and a dedicated S3 bucket with KMS. Recommending SCIM provisioning for ephemeral invites; will validate Okta rate limits.

2026-03-07 - DevSecOps (Security reviewer): Security review required for the seeding templates. Any template with 'vendor' tag triggers manual security sign-off. Also request that audit snapshots be immutably stored with Object Lock (where available).
2026-03-08 - SRE: Noted potential concurrency issue when many claims are approved concurrently; recommend using a queue (SQS) and idempotency token to prevent double-provisioning.
investigation_notes: SCIM vs Okta group invites: SCIM has faster invite flow but requires Okta provisioning setup; alternative is using Slack admin invite API with fallback to manual invites.
Confluence API requires 'site-admin' service account for space creation. We need to scope that account and rotate keys monthly.

Audit snapshot format: JSON with metadata (request_id, approver_id, timestamps), resources created, and a SHA256 signature; retention 7 years for enterprise customers. Need to consult Legal for retention policy variance.
Rate limiting observed in staging when creating >10 spaces in short interval (429 from Confluence). Plan: exponential backoff + per-region rate buckets.
resolution:
Planned rollout path: 1) PoC hardening in staging (1 week): fix service-account scopes, add idempotency tokens, implement SQS queue. 2) Security gating (3 days): template review and Legal sign-off on retention. 3) Canary in prod (us-west) with 3 pilot pods (2 weeks monitoring). 4) Global rollout and automation docs + runbook (follow-up ticket for partner SSO).

Action items created:
- infra: provision s3://redwood-internal-audits/claims + KMS CMK (owner: infra-team).
- auth: create rotated Confluence service account with just-in-time elevation (owner: auth).
- dev: implement queueing and idempotency (owner: automation team).
- sec: review templates and approve vendor gating (owner: DevSecOps).

Post-deployment follow-ups: add fine-grained reporting to Console, add renewal email cadence, and schedule quarterly audit of claimed namespaces. Target full prod rollout by 2026-04-16.
